events.title: The battle of the Maritsa
events.shortBlurb: In a night attack on the Maritsa the Ottomans destroyed the army of the Serbian lords, and the Balkans lay open before them…
body: Since Adrianople had fallen to them about 1361, the Ottoman Turks had pressed into the Balkans. In 1371 the despot Jovan Uglješa and his brother Vukašin, king of Prilep — the two greatest lords of the crumbling Serbian empire of Dušan — gathered a host the chronicles swell to seventy thousand and marched to drive them from Europe.

The Ottoman commander Lala Şahin Pasha had a fraction of their numbers. On the night of 26 September 1371, by the river Maritsa near the village of Chernomen, his men fell upon the Christian camp as it feasted, and the rout was utter: both brothers died on the field, and the victors named the battle Sırp Sındığı, the destruction of the Serbs.

Macedonia and the southern Balkans lay open. Within the year the last Nemanjić emperor, Uroš V, died childless; the Emperor John V of Constantinople became the sultan's tributary; and the road ran on through Kosovo in 1389 and Nicopolis in 1396 to the fall of the imperial city itself in 1453.
